analysis.investment_thesis: CAMS is one of the finest businesses in this batch — ROCE of 53.6%, ROE of 43.9%, 39% operating margins, and a structural tailwind from India's mutual fund AUM growth — but the Magic Formula demands both quality AND cheapness, and at an earnings yield of only ~3.5% (EBIT INR 652 Cr / EV ~INR 18,678 Cr) this is a wonderful business at a stretched price. I admire it; I cannot buy it here.
key_strengths: ROCE of 53.6% and ROE of 43.9% — exceptional capital efficiency powered by an asset-light, near-duopoly RTA model
Operating margin of 39.4% with consistent FCF: INR 359-363 Cr over FY24-25, virtually no capex relative to earnings
Revenue CAGR of 11.6% over 7 years with accelerating growth (INR 910 Cr FY22 → INR 1,422 Cr FY25) as India's MF industry scales
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~3.5% is less than half my 6% minimum threshold — the stock is priced for near-perfection
Zero promoter holding; FII concentration at 44.4% creates vulnerability to foreign capital outflows
P/E of 40x and P/B of 15.25x leave no margin of safety if India's MF AUM growth slows or SEBI changes fee structures
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 28.8x and P/S of 12.6x are valuation multiples that assume many years of flawless execution — any stumble is costly
Regulatory risk: SEBI can reprice or restructure the RTA fee model, directly hitting CAMS' revenue per transaction
No promoter skin-in-the-game (0% promoter holding) — governance reliance on institutional shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The business case for CAMS is genuinely compelling: a structural duopoly (with KFin) processing India's mutual fund transactions, near-zero capital requirements, 53% ROCE, and a direct ride on India's financialization story. FCF conversion is excellent (OCF/net profit ~103%), and the company needs minimal reinvestment to grow. This is the kind of business Greenblatt's formula is built to identify — high ROIC, durable competitive position.

But the Magic Formula is equally ruthless about price. At INR 18,678 Cr EV versus INR 652 Cr EBIT, the earnings yield is 3.5% — a third of what I consider attractive. The market has fully priced in the quality. I would need to see either earnings roughly double from here or the price fall ~40-50% to reach a 7-8% earnings yield that justifies a Magic Formula position. Watch it, want it, but not at today's price.
